title: Introduce Thrifty Defaults Playbook and Quantization Guidance for Unit-Econ Automation
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for opinionated, safe defaults that reduce per-token cost without surprising quality regression. This PR adds a user-facing "Thrifty Defaults Playbook" (YAML templates + prose), a lightweight dry-run CLI that simulates unit-econ impact, and a short quantization guidance doc targeted at product engineers and SREs. Goals: 1) Provide deterministic starter profiles that balance latency and unit cost for common workloads (chat-short, instruction-long, embeddings-heavy). 2) Give a low-friction path to validate defaults via a dry-run that replays sampled traces and reports expected cost/latency deltas. 3) Capture practical quantization heuristics (when to use 4-bit vs 8-bit, calibration signal checks, quality regression checks). Changeset summary: - new docs/playbooks/thrifty-playbook.yaml: three canonical profiles (conservative, balanced, aggressive) with fields for batch_size, prefill_window, kv_cache_policy, quant_profile hints, and fallback model mappings. - cli/cost-dryrun/README.md + small CLI shim cost-dryrun.py: takes a sample workload (ndjson), runs a fast estimator, emits a report and an annotated profile suggestion. - docs/quant/quick-guidance.md: short heuristics, recommended eval set design, and a checklist for canarying quantized models. - core/defaults/selector.go: runtime hooks to pick tenant defaults when not explicitly set and to gracefully opt into playbook-based profiles. - telemetry/schema/update: adds playbook_profile tag and estimated_unit_delta metric for dry-run feedback. Motivation and design details are included inline in docs/playbooks/README.md. Checklist: - [x] YAML starter profiles authored and reviewed - [x] Dry-run CLI implemented with unit tests covering estimator and reporter - [x] Runtime selector integrated and feature-flag guarded - [x] Telemetry fields added and surfaced to Console - [x] Documentation drafted with examples and rollouts How to use: 1) Start with the Conservative profile for new tenants. 2) Run cost-dryrun against a 1k-sample trace to get expected token-cost and p95 latency deltas. 3) If acceptable, promote profile in Console or pin it via tenant config. Safety & fallbacks: profiles include explicit fallback mappings (e.g., if quantized variant entropy > threshold then route to full-precision variant). The runtime selector includes safety gates: do-not-apply if tenant SLAs flagged, and an opt-out metadata key. Backwards compatibility: playbooks are opt-in via a feature flag; the selector defaults to previous conservative behavior when flag is off. Notes on quantization guidance: we recommend calibration sets > 500 samples for chat models with wide token distributions, sample-based KL divergence checks post-quantization, and end-to-end evals on the customer prompt set. CLI dry-run does a cheap simulated tokenization + kernel cost model — it is not an emulator and warns about model-specific microarchitecture variance. Related work: ties to ENG-5123 (tenant defaults), and PM-998 (auto-onboarding economics).
